nodes.name: Qwen3-ASR for speech
nodes.why: Best Hindi + English accuracy in our tests; 0.6B is fast, 1.7B more accurate
nodes.revisit_when: a better offline Hindi model appears

nodes.name: Caption styles: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (CTranslate2 int8) rewrites English only, greedy, 1.5 s limit
nodes.why: Speed test on 30 real lines (M4 Pro): 0.5B median 0.5 s Natural / 0.4 s Simple, never over 1.5 s; 1.5B was nicer but median 1.4 s with 12/30 Natural over 1.5 s. Qwen3-1.7B: fewest rejections but median 1.7 s, 23/30 Natural over 1.5 s. The small model sometimes changes the meaning, so strict checks fall back to word for word
nodes.revisit_when: a faster computer target, or the checks reject too often: try 1.5B (`tests/bench_meaning.py`)

nodes.name: PyTorch is downloaded on first start, not bundled
nodes.why: Keeps installers under 70 MB; picks the GPU build on NVIDIA PCs
nodes.revisit_when: never, unless offline installs are needed

nodes.name: Intel Macs pinned to PyTorch 2.2.2 + NumPy 1.x, CPU only
nodes.why: 2.2.2 is the last Intel Mac build

nodes.name: Intel .pkg built on Apple Silicon via Rosetta
nodes.why: GitHub is retiring its Intel Mac machines

nodes.name: The window is a local web page
nodes.why: Works the same on Mac, Windows and inside OBS; no UI toolkit to install

nodes.name: Google Docs two ways: Way 1 (default) a script in the doc, pasted Web app URL; Way 2 Sign in with Google (OAuth desktop + PKCE, scope drive.file) and the Docs API
nodes.why: Way 1 needs no Google Cloud project and no test list, so anyone can do it; the window names the fix for every wrong paste or deployment setting (the old sidebar link broke with "page not found"). Way 2 makes a new doc per session but the Gmail must be on the test list
nodes.revisit_when: if many users outside the test list want Way 2: publish the app

nodes.name: Desktop app = fork of Handy (Tauri v2), engine stays in Python
nodes.why: The user asked for Handy's UI and features (dictation, history, overlay, tray, onboarding, themes) with our pipeline. Rewriting Qwen3 + NLLB + vocabulary + styles in Rust would have duplicated tested code; a local helper process keeps one pipeline for OBS, the window and dictation
nodes.revisit_when: if the Python install becomes the main support problem

nodes.name: Dictation goes through /dictate, not Handy's Whisper
nodes.why: Same vocabulary, translation and caption style as the captions; Hindi → English while dictating. Handy's models kept as *Built-in* fallback

nodes.name: Handy branding removed; MIT credit kept in About, THIRD_PARTY.md and desktop/LICENSE
nodes.why: User asked to remove the branding; the MIT licence requires the notice

nodes.name: Not signed by Apple/Microsoft
nodes.why: Signing costs money every year; the guide explains the one-time prompt
nodes.revisit_when: if many users get stuck on the prompt
